findings.headline: Your deposited-item return fee is well above the market range.
findings.body: At $10, it is 2× the $5 peer median and the 88th percentile of 16 peers (middle half of the market: $5–$10). This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism.

findings.headline: Smaller premiums elsewhere on the schedule.
findings.body: Your card replacement fee ($15 vs a $10 median, n=11) and your incoming wire fee ($20 vs a $10 median, n=13) also sit above the peer 75th percentile. Individually modest, together they shape how the schedule reads in a side-by-side comparison.

findings.stat_label: comparable lines inside the market range
findings.headline: Most of your schedule is priced with the market.
findings.body: Of the 10 fee lines where we found both your published amount and at least eight comparable peers, six sit between the peer 25th and 75th percentiles, three above and one below.

exec_narrative: Riverside Bank of Dublin is compared with 91 banks under $1B in assets nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index. The size band is wider than usual because fewer than 40 banks in your own size tier have published data; local competitors may price differently. Of 10 rankable lines, six sit inside the middle half of the market, three above it (deposited-item return fee, card replacement fee and incoming wire fee), and one below it (cashier's check fee). We would suggest one step: review the deposited-item return fee, which sits well above the market range; the peer median of $5 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $10
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $5–$10 · range $3–$18 · 88th percentile · n=16
callouts.body: Published as “Returned Deposited Item.” At $10 it is 2× the $5 peer median. This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $5 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Card replacement fee — $15
callouts.stat: Peer median $10 · middle half $5–$12.50 · range $5–$20 · 91st percentile · n=11
callouts.body: Published as “Debit Card Replacement.” At $15 it is $5 above the $10 peer median. It is a small charge, typically incurred after a lost or compromised card, when customers are least forgiving. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $10 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Incoming wire fee — $20
callouts.stat: Peer median $10 · middle half $10–$15 · range $5–$20 · 100th percentile · n=13
callouts.body: Published as “Wire Transfer (Incoming).” At $20 it is 2× the $10 peer median. Charging to receive funds is increasingly uncommon and is noticed by business customers. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $10 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Cashier's check fee — $4
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $5–$7 · 7th percentile · n=14
callouts.body: Published as “Cashier's Check.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $5 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Riverside Bank of Dublin with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
